**ASTRA Health – Intelligent Health Monitoring for Space Missions**

ASTRA Health is an interactive health monitoring platform designed to help astronauts understand and track physiological changes during long-duration space missions.

The application combines a simulated mission monitoring system with real biomedical research data from NASA's Open Science Data Repository (OSD-575), based on the Inspiration4 mission.

Our platform monitors three key health indicators: resting heart rate, sleep duration, and physical activity. It visualizes trends, calculates deviations from individual baseline values, and identifies potential abnormalities using transparent, rule-based alerts. An explainable Mission Health Briefing helps users understand detected changes and suggests appropriate follow-up checks.

Additionally, our NASA Research Explorer enables users to analyze real astronaut biomarker measurements across multiple study timepoints, connecting the prototype to actual space medicine research.

As future missions travel farther from Earth, astronauts may need greater autonomy in monitoring their health. ASTRA Health demonstrates how accessible data visualization, explainable monitoring, and NASA research can support health awareness and informed decision-making in space.

*This prototype uses synthetic mission telemetry and non-medically validated alert thresholds; it is not a diagnostic system.*
details:
ASTRA Health – Explainable Health Monitoring for Space Missions

What Does Our Project Do?

ASTRA Health is an interactive health monitoring prototype designed to help astronauts better understand physiological changes during long-duration space missions.

The platform combines two complementary systems: a simulated Mission Health Dashboard and a NASA Research Explorer using real biomedical data.

1. Mission Health Dashboard

The dashboard simulates a 30-day space mission and monitors three health indicators:

  • Resting heart rate
  • Sleep duration
  • Physical activity

Users can explore different mission days, compare normal and anomalous mission scenarios, and visualize physiological trends through interactive charts.

The system calculates percentage deviations from predefined baseline values and classifies them into three demonstration categories: NORMAL, WARNING, and CRITICAL.

An explainable Mission Health Briefing identifies affected indicators, explains the calculations behind each alert, and suggests cautious follow-up checks.

2. NASA Research Explorer

ASTRA Health integrates real biomedical measurements from NASA's Open Science Data Repository, specifically the OSD-575 dataset from the Inspiration4 mission.

The Research Explorer enables users to examine six blood serum biomarkers, including glucose, creatinine, albumin, sodium, potassium, and total bilirubin.

Measurements from four participants across seven documented sampling occasions can be explored through interactive visualizations.

Original measurement units, missing values, and research metadata are preserved to maintain scientific transparency.

How Does It Address the Challenge?

Long-duration space missions introduce unique health challenges, including physiological changes, isolation, and limited access to immediate medical assistance.

ASTRA Health demonstrates how digital monitoring tools could support astronauts by transforming health measurements into understandable information.

Instead of displaying numbers alone, the platform provides visual trends, baseline comparisons, transparent alert classifications, and explanations of detected changes.

This approach emphasizes explainability and health awareness rather than automated medical diagnosis.

What Are the Benefits and Intended Impact?

Our vision is to contribute toward more autonomous, understandable, and accessible health monitoring technologies for future Moon, Mars, and deep-space missions.

Potential benefits include:

  • Earlier recognition of changes in monitored health indicators.
  • Clearer communication of physiological trends.
  • Transparent explanations supporting informed follow-up decisions.
  • Exploration of authentic NASA biomedical research.
  • A foundation for future integration with real-time sensors and validated medical monitoring protocols.

ASTRA Health could eventually evolve into a more comprehensive mission health support system, subject to scientific validation and appropriate operational safeguards.

Technologies and Development Tools

The prototype was developed using:

  • Python: Core health analysis, data processing, and application logic.
  • Streamlit: Interactive web-based dashboard.
  • Pandas: Processing and validation of health and research datasets.
  • Plotly: Interactive physiological and biomarker visualizations.
  • pytest: Automated testing and validation.
  • NASA Open Science Data Repository: Authentic Inspiration4 biomedical research data.
  • Git and GitHub: Version control and open-source project hosting.
  • OpenAI Codex and ChatGPT: Assistance with implementation, interface design, research, testing, and documentation.

The application runs locally and does not require paid services, external AI APIs, or specialized hardware.

The project repository is publicly available at:

https://github.com/piko000/astra-health

What Makes ASTRA Health Creative?

ASTRA Health combines an interactive mission simulation with authentic space medicine research in one platform.

Its distinguishing feature is the separation of three layers:

  1. Synthetic Mission Telemetry: Demonstrates how daily physiological monitoring might work.
  2. Explainable Alert Logic: Makes every demonstration classification traceable to its underlying measurements and rules.
  3. Real NASA Research Data: Allows users to explore verified biomedical measurements from an actual space mission.

This approach creates an understandable demonstration of future monitoring capabilities while connecting the concept to existing scientific research.

Development Considerations and Limitations

As a solo participant, I prioritized a functional, transparent, and reproducible prototype over unnecessary complexity.

Important considerations included scientific accuracy, data provenance, explainability, accessibility, offline functionality, and software reliability.

The system uses deterministic synthetic mission data and clearly distinguishes them from authentic NASA measurements.

The alert thresholds are demonstration assumptions, not medically validated criteria. The NASA research measurements are presented separately and are not used to generate diagnostic classifications.

The project successfully passed 99 automated tests during development.

ASTRA Health is not a certified medical device or an operational astronaut health system. It demonstrates a possible technical foundation for future research and development.

Our goal is simple: make astronaut health information easier to understand, explore, and act upon responsibly—wherever humanity travels next.
